text: In 2-level type theory (2LTT), the 'inner' and 'outer' type theories serve different purposes:
choices: inner handles computation, outer handles proofs
outer = strict MLTT (for internal rewriting); inner = HoTT (for homotopical content); the outer controls the inner
explanation: 2LTT (Voevodsky, Annenkov-Capriotti-Kraus): two universes — 'fibrant' types (inner) for homotopy and 'strict' types (outer) for bookkeeping. The outer universe has strict UIP; the inner has univalence.
